candidates.current: "Your age." He smiled. "How old did you expect me to be?"
"Fine." He counted silver onto the desk. I should have felt relief. Instead I felt acceleration. I knew that feeling. Hubris putting on its boots.
candidates.following: "If you run," Antonius said, "I find you."

candidates.previous: "Too rich for you?" he asked when I folded.
candidates.current: "Too boring." He stayed in the next hand three raises longer than he should have.

"Income." He looked up.

candidates.previous: "You think your problem is the game."
candidates.current: "It was a gambling loss." He pushed the ledger toward me.
candidates.following: "Your problem is you think being able to explain a mistake means you can afford it." I stared at him. That was annoyingly good.

candidates.current: "No." He paused.
"That's not the same thing." Antonius considered me.
candidates.following: "Interesting opinion from a man whose labor I legally own."

candidates.previous: "Interesting opinion from a man whose labor I legally own."
candidates.current: "Temporarily." He smiled. I swept harder.
candidates.following: The room began separating itself in my head. Not physically. Categories. Recoverable collateral. Unsellable collateral. Broken inventory. Records. Tools. Goods nobody remembered. Things Antonius kept because throwing away something once valued felt like admitting the loan behind it had gone bad. Maybe. That last one was inference. Check. I picked up a brass fitting.

candidates.current: "From where?" Antonius pointed with his broom.
"It wasn't." He came back and picked up the gray frame. I turned one of the stepped plates toward the light.
candidates.following: Three teeth. Where had I seen it? Think. Not enough information yet. But the workmanship was wrong for scrap. Tiny grooves. Matched steps. Reference surfaces rather than moving parts. Precision. Old precision.

candidates.current: "Also correct." He laughed once. "I'll sell you the trash for three silver."
candidates.following: There. Three silver. I could afford that eventually. I could have gotten it free thirty seconds ago. This was already one of the worst negotiations of my second life.

candidates.previous: "So you want to pay three silver for something useless to you."
candidates.current: "I want to pay three silver for something worth forty gold to somebody else. That's called trade. You should look into it." Antonius smiled. I should not have smiled back.
"I am suddenly much less ignorant." He turned the frame over. "Three teeth. Means nothing to me."
"Not enough information yet." He laughed. I hated him.

candidates.previous: "Five and I don't throw it away while you're arguing." I stared at him. He stared back.
candidates.current: "Fine. Five." He put the box on the keep shelf and wrote my name on a scrap tucked beneath it. I pointed. "That's mine."

candidates.previous: "Because, Greg, until thirty seconds ago it was trash."
candidates.current: "Stop saying that." He went back to sweeping. I stared at the Tere gauge.
candidates.following: Forty gold. Maybe more. More than the visible contents of this warehouse put together, if my memory was right. Twenty minutes later I found a cracked wooden case containing six green glass cylinders. My pulse jumped again. Antonius glanced over.

candidates.current: "Wait." He sighed.
candidates.following: The cylinders were cloudy. Each had a metal cap. No mark. I picked one up. Future alchemical storage? Early pressure vessels? Mana cells?

candidates.current: "Was that a test?" He stopped.
candidates.following: The room had become noticeably brighter as we cleared the small window. Dust floated in the beam between us. Antonius rested both hands on the broom.

candidates.current: "Fine." He nodded toward the gray box.

candidates.current: "You actually work." He looked at his dusty hands.

candidates.following: There was no clever answer waiting. That bothered me.

candidates.current: "Antonius." He walked back into the room. I followed.
candidates.following: "You know what everything in your operation does," I said.

candidates.current: "Why?" He picked up a broken stool.
"Fuck you." He laughed.
candidates.following: We found lunch in the front office. Bread. Cheese. Pickled onions. Antonius ate at the clerk's desk because the clerk had gone out. I expected him to have better food. Why? Future Antonius had been rich. Present Antonius had flour. Again. Tower. Bricks. I bit into the bread.

candidates.current: "Yes." He stared. I stared back.

candidates.previous: Not yet. I could lie. Easy. Hard childhood. Older companions. Military upbringing. Dead parents. Some of it even true. Instead I shrugged.
candidates.current: "I had to grow up early." Antonius watched me.
candidates.following: That answer worked on most people because people were polite around dead parents. Antonius was not most people.

candidates.current: "From a lender?" He smiled back.

candidates.following: Then he looked at me for a long moment. Not interrogation. Indexing. I knew the feeling.

candidates.current: "Maybe." He shook his head.

candidates.current: "Do you?" He smiled.

candidates.previous: Then stopped. Why? No reason. No future value. No technical use. No opportunity. I wanted it. That was different.
candidates.current: "Can I have this?" Antonius looked at the scarf.

candidates.previous: "Home." I had never considered that Antonius Vale had a home. That was stupid. Of course he did.
candidates.current: "Where?" He stopped.

candidates.following: "Sunrise tomorrow?" He raised one hand without turning.

candidates.previous: "That's not a no." He walked faster. I laughed.
candidates.current: "Sunrise tomorrow?" He raised one hand without turning.

candidates.previous: "The one where you almost become a person."
candidates.current: "Fuck you." He smiled and kept walking. I followed.

candidates.previous: "Because?" I almost said because I remembered him old.
candidates.current: "Because you have a tired face." He laughed.
candidates.following: We kept walking. The first stop was a cooper's yard. Not the cooper from the green chest. Different man. Antonius spoke with the owner for perhaps six minutes. I expected debt. Instead they discussed barrels. Not prices. Capacity. The cooper had enough work for three months and not enough seasoned wood. Antonius asked how much wood would solve it. The cooper gave a number. Antonius asked what three months of completed barrels would earn.

candidates.current: "Maybe." Antonius looked at me. I had used his word. He smiled.
"Why else?" Antonius kept walking. I followed.

candidates.current: "Assuming he's better." Antonius nodded.

candidates.current: "What do you decide?" He stopped.

candidates.current: "Three from him. Five from you?" Antonius smiled slightly.

candidates.previous: Not my problem to solve. His. He had asked what I thought.
candidates.current: "Then I think the boy is probably worth lending to, but the purchase price may be the bad part of the deal." Antonius nodded.

candidates.following: We walked. Three more stops. A cobbler who did not need money but knew a tanner who did. A widow Antonius paid two silver. That stopped me. She did not sign anything. candidates.current: "Oh." He looked at me.

candidates.previous: Why does he do that? Then watch. This was apparently much easier for me. That was probably insulting. At the tannery, Antonius refused a loan. The tanner was furious. Good shop. candidates.current: "Why no?" Antonius looked pleased.
candidates.following: Not because I asked. Because I had waited.

candidates.current: "Yours is specific." He kept walking. I followed.

candidates.current: "Why?" Antonius shrugged.

candidates.following: "You need everyone to secretly want a kingdom."

candidates.current: "Still." He watched me. I became harmless Greg.
candidates.following: Small smile. Loose shoulders. Young idiot. It happened automatically. Antonius's eyes narrowed. Worse. He had seen the change. Interesting.

candidates.current: "Antonius is surprisingly safe." Antonius put the small ledger on his desk.

candidates.current: "I know that now." Rusk laughed again. Antonius ignored him.

candidates.current: "Yes." He tapped the desk.

candidates.following: "You already remember patterns. Son wants out. Hidden lender. Bad order. Temporary shortage. Structural problem. Write the reason when you refuse. Six months later, see whether you were right." Antonius stared. I felt the branches trying to come.

candidates.following: Categories. Default models. Industry risk. Borrower types. Information network.

candidates.previous: "It's nearly noon." I looked toward the window. It was, in fact, nearly noon.

candidates.previous: "Not until I know what still works."

candidates.following: Arlo set the copper rod down.

candidates.current: "Repeatedly." Arlo frowned. I pointed at the gauntlet. "Can we make it do something?"
"No. You're waiting to see what I say." Antonius smiled slightly.
candidates.following: That was new. A week ago I would have spent the whole appraisal trying to prove I knew more than Arlo. Today I was interested in why Antonius had chosen six gold as the question. Not whether the gauntlet was valuable. Whether it was useful as security. Different. I looked back at the object.

candidates.current: "To whether you should care if it's worth six." Arlo paused.
"If he needs six gold to buy a tavern, that's one problem. If he needs six gold to retrieve the other half of whatever this came from, that's another." Arlo looked at Antonius. Antonius looked at me.
"The object is collateral for the business." Antonius leaned back.
"Useful." Arlo tapped the palm plate with the copper rod. "There's a channel here."
"Blood." Arlo stopped. Antonius stopped. I looked at the gauntlet.
"Don't." Arlo looked at me. I surprised myself too.
"Because if this is a matched system, removing one may tell you what the stone is while destroying the thing that makes the set valuable." Arlo considered.
candidates.following: Then nodded. Antonius noticed. I noticed Antonius noticing. This was becoming ridiculous.

candidates.current: "Excellent." Antonius looked at the ceiling. I smiled.
candidates.following: This was fun. That was dangerous. I knew that now. Not enough to stop. Enough to notice. Arlo found a maker's mark beneath the wrist clasp. Not a symbol. Letters. Very small. He cleaned them with oil.

candidates.previous: Kelvar. Kelven. Maybe I was manufacturing familiarity because I wanted the object to matter. Important. I opened my eyes.
candidates.current: "Not enough information yet." Antonius smiled. Arlo said, "Good." I frowned. "Why good?"
"Frequently." Arlo returned to the mark.

candidates.previous: "If I remembered, I'd have said it."
candidates.current: "Reasonable." Antonius stood.
candidates.following: "Can either of you tell me whether I should lend six gold against it?"

candidates.current: "Yours sounds expensive." Antonius sat again.
candidates.following: "How?" I looked at the gauntlet. Then at Arlo.

candidates.previous: "How?" I looked at the gauntlet. Then at Arlo.
candidates.current: "Registry." Arlo nodded.
"Why?" Antonius looked at me.

candidates.previous: "The borrower has repaid you twice. One late payment had a verifiable external cause. He already has four gold committed, so he has something to lose. A competent artificer with an incentive to undervalue this still offered three gold and claims eight to fifteen if complete. Even if he's lying downward, the object has a market. Even if he's lying upward because he wants the borrower to sell, his three-gold offer establishes a floor unless he's willing to withdraw it." Antonius said, "He might."
candidates.current: "Then call him on it before lending." Arlo smiled. I was enjoying myself.
"Yes." Arlo looked at me.

candidates.previous: Not mine. I looked at Antonius.
candidates.current: "That's my answer." He tapped the desk.
"Five." Arlo raised an eyebrow. Antonius said, "Why five?"

"Because I don't know what the wrist stones do." Antonius looked at the object in his hands. Then at Arlo. Then very carefully put it down. I laughed so hard I had to sit. Antonius waited. I tried to stop.

candidates.previous: "Five gold," he said. "Expedition share first claim. Gauntlet secondary. Subject to the artificer's three-gold offer remaining open." I wiped my eyes.
candidates.current: "Good." Antonius pointed at me.
candidates.following: "You are not coming." I stopped laughing.

candidates.current: "Exactly." Antonius picked up his ledger.
candidates.following: Meeting over. I stayed seated. He looked at me.

candidates.current: "I need you to inspect it." Arlo paused. Antonius looked annoyed.

candidates.current: "Also educational." Hessa pointed to the mat. I sat.

There was no dignified way to describe sitting cross-legged while trying to persuade a body to notice something my mind remembered as obvious. Mana had once been everywhere. Not metaphorically. I had felt it in rooms, people, spells, stone, weather, bad enchantments, good enchantments, wounds, monsters, and the peculiar pressure behind the eyes that meant somebody nearby was doing something clever and probably irresponsible.

candidates.current: "That's why barely seemed appropriate." She stared at me. I smiled.
"Very." She sat opposite me.
"Antonius lent five." Arlo nodded.
"Too late." He put down his tool.
"Probably." He opened the box. The gray hook.
candidates.following: Two rods. Tiny square plates. Three-tooth mark. Arlo stopped joking. That was satisfying. He lifted one rod. Carefully. Turned it.

candidates.current: "Same number of useful syllables." Arlo looked at me.
"Antonius had the debtor record." Arlo set the rod down.
"Calibration gauge." Arlo looked offended.

candidates.previous: Possibly more. Arlo was breathing differently. I noticed.
candidates.current: "How valuable?" He did not answer.
"No. Greg." He looked at me.
"No one." Arlo closed the box.
"Forty?" He laughed.
"How much?" Arlo looked at the box.
"What could you do?" He leaned back.
"Mostly." He laughed. I put both hands on the table.
candidates.following: "What do you need from me?" Arlo frowned.

candidates.previous: "Mostly." He laughed. I put both hands on the table.
candidates.current: "What do you need from me?" Arlo frowned.
candidates.following: That was not the question he expected.

candidates.previous: "Then what?" I looked at the box. Then at Arlo.
candidates.current: "Use it." He went still.
candidates.following: Not dramatically. Arlo was not dramatic. His stillness was smaller. More expensive.

candidates.current: "To test it without damaging it." Arlo looked at me for a long moment. Then at the box.
"One gold?" He laughed.
"I'll cover six." He stared. I stared back.
candidates.following: Then remembered I did not have six silver.

"Momentum." She laughed. I disliked how often people laughed when I used that word. Hessa sat opposite me. "Tell me what you did."

"That's one purpose." Hessa stared at me for several seconds. Then she stood. "Go home."
"That's because you interrupted at a delicate moment." Rusk held up a folded paper.

candidates.current: "Pick up what?" Rusk shrugged.
"Difference?" Rusk turned toward the stairs.
candidates.following: "Wait." He stopped. I held up one finger.

candidates.current: "Wait." He stopped. I held up one finger.
candidates.following: "Yesterday I cast Barrier." Rusk looked at the finger. Then at me.

candidates.current: "Yesterday I cast Barrier." Rusk looked at the finger. Then at me.

candidates.previous: "Did you do magic with the boxes?" I stopped.
candidates.current: "How could you possibly know that?" Rusk smiled.
candidates.following: "You told me you cast Barrier, then I sent you to move something heavy. You're Greg."

candidates.current: "Oil." Antonius looked at Rusk. Rusk said, "Magic." Antonius looked back at me.
"Potential." Antonius sighed.
candidates.following: "Keep it out of the ledger until it pays for something."

candidates.current: "Good." He handed me another paper. I looked at it.
"No." Antonius leaned back.

candidates.current: "Thank you." Antonius blinked. Rusk looked over. I frowned. "What?"

candidates.previous: "I was trying to get you out."
candidates.current: "Still data." Arlo looked at the coins. Then at me.

"Fine." He took three silver. Pushed three back. I looked at them.
"No." She stared. I sat on the mat.
"So." Hessa sighed.
candidates.following: "You are going to do this whether I help."

candidates.current: "Air touches it." She stared.
"That's not a number." He looked at me. I smiled. He looked back at the regulators.

"Not this one." He laughed despite himself. Then his face changed. Not joy. Worry. I knew that too.

candidates.following: "One regulator," I said. He looked at me.

candidates.current: "Then learn that while making one." Arlo stared at me. I enjoyed this far too much.

candidates.current: "Not tomorrow." Antonius smiled.

candidates.current: "Somewhat." Antonius returned to his ledger. Then said, "The salvager came back." Everything in me changed. I hated that he noticed.

candidates.previous: "Carrow is not the size of a kingdom."
